meaning.evidence: Every point survives, commands and links intact: "you shouldn't expect big formatting changes down the track", "If you're feeling confident, use `--fast`."

sense.evidence: "fiddly bits", "Have a squiz", "get cracking", "down the track" fit; "no-nonsense" is a little softer than "uncompromising", which is the project's point.

authenticity.evidence: Natural Australian English in a README voice: "grab one of the PyInstaller-built standalone executables", "brainpower for the stuff that actually matters".

register.evidence: A light level 2 touch: "squiz", "get cracking", "down the track", otherwise plain. No swearing.

tone.evidence: Stays a confident, practical README: "Black makes code review quicker by producing the smallest diffs possible."

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "After a while the formatting stops being something you notice, and you can focus on the content instead."

variety.evidence: Varied, though a reader sees "have a look" and "Have a squiz" doing the same job; "fiddly bits", "grab", "get cracking", "down the track".

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the Black README, with its "Any colour you like." motto.

A.summary: Light, natural and faithful; right on the brief.

meaning.evidence: Every point survives: "Now that we're stable, don't go expecting big formatting changes down the track."; "One more thing:" is colour.

sense.evidence: "the Python code formatter that won't budge" catches "uncompromising"; "Heaps of projects", "the full rundown", "have a squiz" fit.

authenticity.evidence: Sounds like an Australian developer writing: "Want to format Jupyter Notebooks as well?", "just grab one of the PyInstaller-built standalone executables".

register.evidence: Light level 2 touch, a shade chattier than A: "won't budge", "Heaps", "squiz", "don't go expecting". No swearing.

tone.evidence: Keeps the confident, practical README tone: "If you're feeling confident, use `--fast`."

flow.evidence: Reads like it was written that way: "After a while you stop even noticing the formatting, and you can get on with the content instead."

variety.evidence: Varied with nothing leaned on: "won't budge", "fiddly bits", "get cracking", "Heaps", "down the track", "rundown", "squiz".

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the Black README; "won't budge" keeps its uncompromising character.

problems.quote: _Black_ is the Python code formatter that won't budge.
problems.original: _Black_ is the uncompromising Python code formatter.
problems.why: Good fit, though it moves the project's tagline word out of its usual slot.

B.summary: Natural, faithful and varied; the best of the set.

meaning.evidence: Every point survives: "Black checks that the reformatted code still produces a valid AST".

sense.evidence: "heaps of projects", "have a squiz", "get cracking" fit; "Now that we've gone stable" strains (projects "become" stable, "gone" suggests a switch), and "no-nonsense" softens "uncompromising".

authenticity.evidence: Natural Australian English: "grab one of the PyInstaller-built standalone executables", "down the track".

register.evidence: Light level 2 touch: "heaps", "squiz", "get cracking", "down the track". No swearing.

tone.evidence: Keeps the practical README tone throughout.

flow.evidence: Mostly smooth, but "After a while the formatting stops getting noticed" is a clumsy passive.

problems.quote: After a while the formatting stops getting noticed
problems.original: Formatting becomes transparent after a while
Now that we have become stable

C.summary: Light and faithful, a little less polished than A.

meaning.evidence: The steps survive, but "Sign up for it" implies a subscription, and "Less to wade through, less to argue about." adds a claim the original does not make; "Easy as." is colour.

sense.evidence: Several terms strain: "won't take no for an answer" means pushy, not uncompromising; "churning out the smallest diffs possible" suggests mass output where the point is minimal change; "Sign up for it" for "By using it".

authenticity.evidence: Plenty of natural idiom ("banging on at you", "won't play ball", "Feeling game?"), but packed so densely it starts to read as a showcase: "a stack more info", "the nitty-gritty", "Easy as."

register.evidence: Heavier than a level 2: idioms in almost every sentence ("hand over the reins", "get stuck into", "shake-ups", "Feeling game?") plus added tags. No swearing.

tone.evidence: Still a README, but the stream of quips ("Easy as.", "Less to wade through, less to argue about.") makes it breezier than the original's crisp confidence.

flow.evidence: Readable, but the density of idiom piles up: "Sign up for it and you're agreeing to hand over the reins on all the fiddly little bits of hand-formatting."

variety.evidence: Very varied: "banging on", "get stuck into", "won't play ball", "a stack more", "shake-ups", "nitty-gritty".

essence.evidence: Recognisably the Black README, but "won't take no for an answer" turns principled rigidity into pushiness.

problems.quote: the Python code formatter that won't take no for an answer
problems.why: Wrong sense: pushy insistence rather than refusal to compromise on style.

problems.quote: churning out the smallest diffs possible
problems.why: 'Churning out' implies volume and carelessness, against the point.

problems.quote: Less to wade through, less to argue about.

problems.why: Tag bolted on; part of the over-weighting.

D.summary: Colourful and varied but over the brief, with several terms in the wrong sense.

meaning.evidence: The original word for word: "By using it, you agree to cede control over minutiae of hand-formatting."

sense.evidence: No Aussie terms to misfire; only the spelling in "Any colour you like." changes.

authenticity.evidence: Plain international English with no Australian voice at all: "Further information can be found in our docs".

register.evidence: Untranslated apart from "colour"; nowhere near a level 2 light touch.

variety.evidence: No slang at all to vary.

problems.original: _Black_ is the uncompromising Python code formatter. By using it, you agree to cede
